methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $15M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 2 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 13 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

methods.name: Public-Comp Anchoring
methods.skip_reason: target revenue not on file (private companies rarely disclose)
methods.rationale: Public Semiconductors P/S median is 18.9x across 3 tickers. Cannot apply without target's revenue.

data.narrative:
Fab2, a seed-stage semiconductor company founded by Jim Keller and Sam Zeloof, has raised $15M+ to date. The Chips & Semiconductors sector includes a peer universe of 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers including Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, and SambaNova Systems. However, the narrow-filter peer set lacks sufficient depth for reliable median-based valuation.

Stage-progression valuation is the only applicable triangulation method. Using total capital raised ($15M) as a proxy for entry valuation and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $38M. Public semiconductor comps trade at a 18.9x median price-to-sales multiple, but this cannot be applied without revenue disclosure from the target. Peer-median analysis is inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage private comparables meeting minimum sample thresholds.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $32M to $43M, centered at $38M. This range reflects a ±15% variance band around the stage-progression midpoint. Key uncertainties include the actual deployment capital versus equity raised, burn rate trajectory, and technical differentiation relative to the identified private peer set. Revenue traction and IP defensibility remain critical inputs for future revaluation as the company progresses toward Series A.
